name: HD44780
full_name: Hitachi HD44780U Dot-Matrix Character LCD Controller/Driver
description: The HD44780 is the de facto standard controller behind nearly every monochrome character LCD module (16x2, 20x4, etc.). Hobbyists almost never touch the bare chip; they wire the 16-pin module header it sits behind. The parallel interface can run in 8-bit mode (D0-D7) or 4-bit mode (D4-D7 only) to save four MCU pins, with RS/RW/E as the control lines. Contrast is set with an analog voltage on V0, usually from a trimpot between VDD and VSS. Its 4-bit mode and the universally cloned instruction set make decades-old code and libraries work on virtually any compatible module.

pins.name: V0
pins.description: contrast adjust input; set with a trimpot between VDD and VSS

pins.name: RW
pins.description: read/write select: 0 = write, 1 = read; tie to GND if only writing

pins.name: E
pins.description: enable strobe; data latched on the falling edge

pins.name: D4
pins.description: data bit 4 (used in both 4-bit and 8-bit modes)

pins.name: D5
pins.description: data bit 5 (used in both 4-bit and 8-bit modes)

pins.name: D6
pins.description: data bit 6 (used in both 4-bit and 8-bit modes)

pins.name: D7
pins.description: data bit 7 (used in both modes; also the busy flag when read)

pins.name: A
pins.description: backlight LED anode (LED+); usually needs a series current-limiting resistor

typical_application: Driving a 16x2 or 20x4 character LCD from a microcontroller in 4-bit mode, with a 10k trimpot on V0 for contrast and a resistor in series with pin 15 (A) for the backlight.
gotchas: in 4-bit mode only D4-D7 are wired; D0-D3 are left unconnected
E is a strobe, not a clock line you free-run; data is latched on its falling edge
tie RW to GND if you never read; reading is rarely needed and forgetting it can drive the bus against the MCU
no contrast voltage on V0 (or wrong polarity) shows a blank screen or only black boxes, often mistaken for a dead module
backlight pin 15 (A) needs an external series resistor on most bare modules to avoid burning out the LED
